headline: Secure Parkway and Event Stays Early
reservation: While Boone itself requires no entry permit, Blue Ridge Parkway activities are separate from ticketed attractions like Grandfather Mountain, which require distinct booking. Popular fall weekends and university events often fill local lodging months in advance; verify all specific venue systems via official channels as policies are subject to change.

days.title: Town Intro and High Country Views

stops.name: Downtown Boone
stops.detail: Walk the shops and galleries near Appalachian State University to acclimate to the mountain atmosphere.

stops.name: Boone Greenway
stops.detail: Choose this accessible path for a low-impact introduction to local scenery before heading higher.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local town loops; conditions vary by university traffic.
days.note: Expect higher activity levels during university events and graduation weekends.

days.title: Parkway Heritage and Water Trails

stops.name: Moses H. Cone Memorial Park
stops.detail: Walk the historic carriage roads for gentle grades and pastoral views of the estate.

stops.name: Julian Price Memorial Park
stops.detail: Complete the Price Lake loop for woodland and water vistas, keeping an eye out for roots and mud.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; mountain roads require slower speeds and focused attention.
days.note: Check the official NPS parkway page for seasonal road closures or facility maintenance.

days.title: Rugged Ridges and Engineering Marvels

stops.name: Rough Ridge
stops.detail: A steeper, rocky climb providing expansive views of the surrounding peaks when visibility allows.

stops.name: Linn Cove Viaduct
stops.detail: Visit the visitor center to learn about this complex bridge that hugs the mountain slopes.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the round trip; weather and fog can significantly slow travel.
days.note: Ridge-top temperatures are often much cooler than town; carry extra layers.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at Rough Ridge and Price Lake fills rapidly on summer and fall weekends. Arrive early or have a secondary town-based plan if lots are at capacity.

intel.title: Mountain Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is frequently interrupted along the Blue Ridge Parkway and deeper trail sections. Download navigation maps for offline use before leaving Boone.

intel.title: Strategic Refueling
intel.text: Fuel is not available directly on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Ensure your tank is sufficient in Boone or Blowing Rock before beginning scenic loops.

intel.title: Seasonal Pacing
intel.text: Fall color timing varies by elevation and can change weekly. Suggested morning starts help avoid the heaviest afternoon traffic near Blowing Rock.

intel.title: Weather Flexibility
intel.text: Dense fog can make ridge driving hazardous and eliminate views. If visibility is low, shift plans to Boone's indoor galleries or downtown shops.

plan.arrival: Pick up your rental at TRI airport and allow roughly 100 minutes to reach Boone. Check into your base, then explore downtown for supplies and dinner.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is suitable for main roads, but check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved mountain access.
plan.goldenHour: Rough Ridge offers a classic viewpoint, though sunset clarity depends heavily on seasonal cloud cover.
